capture.metricsSource: Guest capture helper: the isolated two-vCPU Linux guest's /proc/stat, /proc/meminfo and /proc/pressure/*
capture.transitionSource: Bullseye state.json; first observation of each runId/version
capture.logSource: Verbatim allowlisted Bullseye stdout; timestamps observed inside the Linux guest when each stdout line was read, preserved to milliseconds; not Docker receive times
capture.transitionTiming: atMs is first capture time; sinceMs is the agent's state-transition time
capture.evidenceMeaning: Evidence recorded at a diagnostic transition, not continuous telemetry
notes: Recorded run in a genuine separate Linux kernel with exactly two online vCPUs under QEMU TCG; not live monitoring.
The original Bullseye configuration is unchanged, including 5-second sampling, CPU and PSI thresholds, and 30-second recovery duration.
CPU load is confined to the isolated guest; metrics use the guest's own /proc counters, not Docker host totals or synthesized counters.
Software-emulated diagnostic experiment, not a production throughput or capacity benchmark.
The replay chart begins after agent and workload warmup; earlier startup stdout is retained separately in preludeLogs with its original timestamps.
The gradual CPU workload is controlled inside the guest; this is not captured HTTP traffic or a production traffic replay.
Continuous metrics come from an auxiliary /proc sampler, not a Bullseye continuous metrics export.
Bullseye evidence belongs to recorded state transitions; no events or measurements are interpolated.
agentRevision identifies the base commit; agentWorkingTreeDirty records whether local source changes were present.
